newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 9.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Political parties are to meet by Thursday to - either informally or in the Constitutional Assembly management committee - to begin planning the complex task of redrafting the constitution in line with the requirements of the Constitutional court.

- The Inkatha Freedom Party national council had not met to discuss the possibility of returning to the Constitutional Assembly at its meeting on Saturday as the party still needed time to study the Constitutional Court's ruling on the national constitution and KwaZulu/Natal constitution.

- South Africa's partners in the Southern African Customs Union fear the European Unions's negotiating mandate for a free trade agreement with South Africa will have devastating effects on their economies.

- Nethold, the international pay-TV company jointly owned by Richemont SA RIFX.S and MIH Ltd , has been split into two and its European interests merged with French pay-TV group Canal+ , to create one of the world's largest pay-television groups.
- South Africa's gold and foreign exchange reserves fell 2.9 percent or 292 million rand in August to 10,078 billion rand from July's 10.37 billion, continuing a downward trend.

- The sale of Nethold, the South African owned and Netherlands-based pay-television group, to Canal Plus, a French-based pay-television operator last week, values Nethold at considerably less than the deal shareholders were expecting to be announced between Nethold and Hughes Electronics of the U.S.

- Nethold executives remained tightlipped about the outcome of reported negotiations with Hughes Electronics, the General motors subsidiary, after the announcement on Friday that Canal Plus, the French pay-television operator would buy Nethold.

- Doubts have been raised about an agreement of intent the Maize Board signed with Taiwan last week to export maize to that country until 1999, amid expectations among board officials that the maize body would cease to exist in a year's time.
- South Africa's gross gold and foreign exchange reserves dropped a modest 292 million rand last month to a record their lowest level since the 1994 elections, the Reserve Bank said on Friday.
- The Sandton rates boycott comes to a head this week with provincial and local authorities having finally agreed to meet ratepayers to discuss the 243 percent rates increases.
